sections.title: Expressing causes
sections.content:
Advanced ways to explain why something happens:
• stem from — originate from. Many health problems stem from poor diet.
• trigger — cause something to begin. The announcement triggered widespread protests.
• attribute to — regard as caused by. She attributed her success to hard work.
• give rise to — cause to happen. Rapid urbanisation has given rise to housing shortages.
• owing to — because of (formal). The match was cancelled owing to heavy rain.

sections.title: Expressing effects
sections.content:
Describing outcomes and consequences:
• consequently — as a result. Sales dropped; consequently, staff were laid off.
• bring about — cause to happen. New technology has brought about major changes.
• impact — have a strong effect on. Climate change impacts agriculture worldwide.
• repercussion — an unintended consequence. The policy had serious economic repercussions.
• ramification — a complex consequence. The legal ramifications of this decision are enormous.

exercises.question: 'Many problems stem from poverty' means poverty is the:
exercises.explanation: Stem from means to originate from or be caused by.

exercises.question: An unintended negative consequence is a:
exercises.explanation: A repercussion is an unintended consequence of an action.

exercises.question: 'Owing to bad weather, the flight was delayed' — 'owing to' means:
exercises.explanation: Owing to is a formal way of saying 'because of'.

exercises.question: To cause something to start suddenly is to:
exercises.explanation: Trigger means to cause an event or situation to happen.

exercises.question: 'She attributed her success to luck' means she:
exercises.hint: She credited luck for her success.
exercises.explanation: Attribute to means to regard something as being caused by.

exercises.question: 'Consequently' is closest in meaning to:
exercises.explanation: Consequently means as a result or therefore.

exercises.question: Complex, far-reaching consequences of a decision are:
exercises.explanation: Ramifications are complex or unwelcome consequences of an action.

exercises.question: To 'bring about' change means to:
exercises.explanation: Bring about means to cause something to happen.
